_note: EXAMPLE ONLY — a candidate requirement, not an approved or implemented feature. human_decision is PENDING.
problem: Context behind a glucose change is often missing for seniors who cannot recall meals/insulin.
user_outcome: A senior can optionally record simple context (meal / drink / insulin) with a one-tap YES / NO / I DON'T REMEMBER, without pressure to remember.

solution_options.summary: Optional, dismissible contextual question card after a notable change, answerable YES / NO / I DON'T REMEMBER.
cons: Needs careful timing to avoid nagging

solution_options.summary: Always-visible quick 'log context' buttons on the Senior home.

counterargument: Any context prompt risks nagging or implying the app expects an action; must be strictly optional and never coercive.
safety_implications: Must obey SAFETY_GUARDRAILS.md G1 (no dose recommendation), G3 (provenance: user-entered fact), and G5 (tolerate 'I DON'T REMEMBER'). The card may only capture context; it must never suggest a specific insulin dose.
acceptance_criteria: Given a notable change, when a context card appears, then it offers YES / NO / I DON'T REMEMBER and can be dismissed.
Given the user selects 'I DON'T REMEMBER', when saved, then the event is stored as user-entered with unknown value and no dose is ever suggested.
test_plan: Unit-test that the card model exposes exactly YES / NO / I DON'T REMEMBER and a dismiss action.
Static safety check: no dose-recommendation string is produced by the context feature.
